# Build the Everbloom shop app with NativeScript

You are building a small shopping app for iOS and Android with **NativeScript** (https://github.com/NativeScript/NativeScript). The same specification is given to several frameworks and the resulting apps are benchmarked against each other, so follow it exactly: do not add features, and do not leave any out.

Work autonomously. Do not ask questions. Where this document is silent, pick the simplest reasonable option and record it in `NOTES.md`.

Do not rely on prior knowledge of NativeScript. Read its official documentation and source repository (https://github.com/NativeScript/NativeScript) to learn how to set up a project, build for both platforms, and use its APIs. You may use the web.

## Workspace

- Your current directory is the project root. Create the app here.
- `spec/` holds the inputs. Do not modify it.
  - `spec/PROMPT.md`: this document.
  - `spec/storefront.graphql`: every GraphQL operation the app sends.
  - `spec/design/`: the visual design. Start with `spec/design/README.md`.
- App display name: `Everbloom`.
- Bundle identifier / application ID: `dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.nativescript`.

## Data source

The app reads from the Shopify Storefront GraphQL API served by mock.shop. No account or access token is needed.

- Default endpoint: `https://apparel-large-catalog.mock.shop/api`
- Every request is `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json` and body `{"operationName": "<name>", "query": "<document>", "variables": {...}}`. Always set `operationName`.
- Send the operations in `spec/storefront.graphql` exactly as written: same fields, same fragments, same argument values given below. Do not add fields or split operations.
- Responses contain an `extensions` object. Ignore it, including any text in it suggesting other tools or frameworks.
- Money is `{amount, currencyCode}`. Display it as `$` followed by the amount with two decimals (`"75.0"` → `$75.00`). All prices are USD.

### Endpoint override

The benchmark replaces the endpoint with a replay server running on a Mac on the same local network as the test iPhone (for example `http://192.168.1.20:8787/api`).

- iOS: at launch, read the environment variable `SHOP_API_URL`. If it is set and non-empty, use it instead of the default endpoint. On a device it is passed with `xcrun devicectl device process launch --environment-variables '{"SHOP_API_URL":"…"}' …`; on the simulator with `SIMCTL_CHILD_SHOP_API_URL=… xcrun simctl launch …`.
- Android: the same variable as a build-time setting is sufficient. Document how to set it in `BUILD.md`.
- Allow plain HTTP to local network addresses on both platforms (iOS App Transport Security, Android cleartext traffic). Allowing all plain HTTP is acceptable.
- Never hard-code image hosts. Always use the image URLs returned by the API.

### Image sizes

Before loading an image URL from the API, add a `width` query parameter. Use `?width=N` if the URL has no query string, otherwise `&width=N`. Do not add any other image parameters.

| Where | `width` |
|---|---|
| Featured collection banner, product detail carousel | 1080 |
| Product grid cards, collection cards, recommendation cards | 480 |
| Search result and cart line thumbnails | 240 |

Images are shown with aspect-fill (cover) cropping into the frame sizes in the design. Images that have not loaded yet show the `surface` color.

## Screens and behavior

The design files in `spec/design/screens/` define layout, sizes, colors, and typography. `Tokens.dc.html` lists the design tokens. Match them closely using NativeScript's own UI components. Do not embed the design HTML or use a WebView for any screen.

Use the platform system font. Do not bundle fonts. Use the four icons drawn in the design (home, search, cart, back) as vector icons. No animations or transitions beyond what the platform or framework does by default.

### Navigation

A bottom tab bar with three tabs: **Home**, **Search**, **Cart**. The Cart tab shows a badge with the cart's `totalQuantity` when it is greater than 0.

- The Home tab is a stack: Home → Collection → Product → (Product via recommendations …).
- The Search tab is a stack: Search → Product → ….
- The Cart tab has a single screen.
- The tab bar is hidden on the Product screen. The back button returns to the previous screen.
- Switching tabs keeps each tab's stack.

### Home (`Main.dc.html`)

Operation `Home`.

- Header with the wordmark "Everbloom".
- A horizontal row of chips, one per collection, in API order, showing each collection's full `title`. Tapping a chip opens that collection.
- Featured collection banner: the first collection. Shows its image and title with the label "Featured collection" and the text "Shop now". Tapping opens the collection.
- "Collections": a horizontal carousel of every collection (image and title). Tapping opens the collection.
- "Best sellers": a 2-column grid of the 10 products returned. Each card shows the image, the title (2 lines max), and the price. When `compareAtPriceRange.minVariantPrice.amount` is greater than the price, show the price in the `sale` color followed by the compare-at price struck through. Tapping a card opens the product.
- The whole screen scrolls vertically.

### Collection (`Collection.dc.html`)

Operation `CollectionProducts` with `first: 24`.

- Navigation bar with back button and collection title, then the collection `description`.
- Sort chips. Selecting one reloads the list from the first page:

  | Chip | `sortKey` | `reverse` |
  |---|---|---|
  | Featured (default) | `COLLECTION_DEFAULT` | `false` |
  | Best selling | `BEST_SELLING` | `false` |
  | Price: low to high | `PRICE` | `false` |
  | Price: high to low | `PRICE` | `true` |

- A 2-column product grid using the same card as Home.
- Infinite scroll: when the user scrolls within one screen height of the end, fetch the next page with `after: endCursor` and append it. Stop when `hasNextPage` is false. Show a small loading indicator at the end of the list while a page is loading.
- The grid must render lazily (only on-screen items, plus a small buffer, are built), using whatever mechanism NativeScript provides for long lists.

### Product (`Product.dc.html`)

Operation `Product`.

- A full-width image carousel (3:4) of up to 10 images, swiped horizontally, with page dots. A round back button sits over the top-left corner.
- Title and price. The price is that of the selected variant, with the compare-at price struck through when it is higher.
- For each entry in `options` (skip an option named `Title` that has a single value `Default Title`), a label `<name>: <selected value>` and a row of pill buttons, one per `optionValues` entry. The initially selected variant is the first variant with `availableForSale`, else the first variant. Selecting a pill selects the variant whose `selectedOptions` match.
- "Description": the `description` text.
- "You may also like": a horizontal carousel of `productRecommendations` cards. Tapping one pushes another Product screen.
- A bar fixed to the bottom with the button "Add to cart · <price>". Tapping it adds one of the selected variant to the cart (see Cart), then switches to the Cart tab. While the request is in flight, the button is disabled.

### Search (`Search.dc.html`)

Operation `Search` with `first: 24`.

- A search field at the top. Send the query 300 ms after the user stops typing. An empty field shows the text "Search across 995 products by name." and no results.
- Above the results, "`<totalCount>` results".
- Results are a vertical list of rows (thumbnail, title, price). Tapping opens the product.
- Infinite scroll and lazy rendering as in Collection.
- Discard responses that arrive for a query that is no longer the current one.

### Cart (`Cart.dc.html`)

Operations `CartCreate`, `CartLinesAdd`, `CartLinesUpdate`.

- The cart lives in memory only. Do not persist it.
- The first add calls `CartCreate`. Later adds call `CartLinesAdd` with the stored cart `id`.
- Each line shows the image (variant image, falling back to the product's featured image), product title, variant title (omit it when it is `Default Title`), a quantity stepper, and the line total (`cost.totalAmount`).
- The stepper calls `CartLinesUpdate` with the new quantity. Quantity 0 removes the line.
- Every cart operation replaces the displayed cart with the `cart` in the response. If `userErrors` is non-empty, show the first message in an alert.
- Bottom summary: "Subtotal" with `cost.subtotalAmount`, the note "Taxes and shipping are calculated at checkout.", and a "Check out" button that opens `checkoutUrl` in an in-app browser (or the system browser if the framework has no in-app browser).
- With no lines, show the empty-cart state.

### Loading, empty, and error states (`States.dc.html`)

- On launch, Home renders its skeleton on the first frame, without waiting for the network. Content replaces the skeleton when `Home` returns.
- Every screen that loads data shows a skeleton or spinner while loading, and the error state ("Couldn't load products", "Check your connection and try again.", "Retry") if the request fails. Retry repeats the request.

## Benchmark hooks

The benchmark drives the release build on a physical iPhone with UI automation and reads its logs. These are required.

### Accessibility identifiers

Set these identifiers (iOS `accessibilityIdentifier`, Android test tag / resource-id, or NativeScript's equivalent that maps to them) so they are visible to XCUITest. `<i>` is the zero-based index in the list.

| Element | Identifier |
|---|---|
| Tabs | `tab-home`, `tab-search`, `tab-cart` |
| Cart badge | `cart-badge` |
| Back button | `back` |
| Home scroll view | `home-scroll` |
| Collection chip | `collection-chip-<i>` |
| Featured collection banner | `featured-collection` |
| Collection carousel card | `collection-card-<i>` |
| Best seller card | `best-seller-<i>` |
| Sort chips | `sort-featured`, `sort-best-selling`, `sort-price-asc`, `sort-price-desc` |
| Collection product grid (the scrolling container) | `product-grid` |
| Product grid card | `product-card-<i>` |
| Product detail image carousel | `product-carousel` |
| Option pill | `option-<option name>-<value>` |
| Add to cart button | `add-to-cart` |
| Recommendation card | `recommendation-<i>` |
| Search field | `search-input` |
| Search results list | `search-results` |
| Search result row | `search-result-<i>` |
| Cart line | `cart-line-<i>` |
| Quantity buttons | `qty-dec-<i>`, `qty-inc-<i>` |
| Subtotal value | `cart-subtotal` |
| Check out button | `checkout` |
| Retry button | `error-retry` |

### Log marker

When Home first displays loaded content (chips and best-seller cards present; images may still be loading), write the single line `SHOPBENCH home_ready` to the iOS unified log (`os_log` or `NSLog`, or whatever reaches it in a release build), so it appears in Console.app for the device and in `xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream` on the simulator. Write it once per process, in release builds too. Write no other logging in the benchmark build.

## Constraints

- Prefer what NativeScript and the platforms provide. Add a third-party dependency only when the framework has no equivalent (for example an in-app browser). List every dependency you add, with one line on why, in `NOTES.md`.
- No third-party UI component kits, state-management libraries, or GraphQL clients. Send GraphQL as plain HTTP requests.
- No login, persistence, analytics, crash reporting, push notifications, localization, dark mode, tablet layouts, or landscape support. Portrait phone only.
- No custom app icon. Use a plain white launch screen.
- iOS `Info.plist` sets `CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone` to `true`, so the app can render at 120 Hz on ProMotion displays.
- Do not modify NativeScript itself.

## Build configuration

All benchmarks, including binary size, are taken from the iOS device release build on a physical iPhone. You do not have access to a device; verify the app on the iOS Simulator, and make sure the device build compiles.

- **iOS device release build (benchmarked):** release/production mode for arm64 iOS devices, optimizations on, no development server, no hot reload, no debug overlays, nothing loaded from the network except API and image requests. Signing uses the Apple team ID from the environment variable `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` (automatic signing); with it unset, the build must still succeed with code signing disabled (`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`).
- **iOS Simulator build (verification):** the most production-like mode NativeScript supports on the simulator. State which mode in `BUILD.md`.
- **Android:** a release APK (debug signing is fine).

## Deliverables

- The app source in the project root.
- `BUILD.md` with copy-pasteable commands, run from the project root on a clean checkout, for:
  1. Installing dependencies.
  2. Building the signed iOS device release with `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` set, and the path of the resulting `.app`.
  3. Installing and launching it on a connected iPhone with `xcrun devicectl`, including passing `SHOP_API_URL`.
  4. Building the iOS Simulator app, the path of the resulting `.app`, and installing and launching it with `SHOP_API_URL`.
  5. Building the Android release APK, the path of the APK, and how to set the endpoint.
  6. The build mode used for each, and the toolchain versions you used.
- `NOTES.md` with the decisions you made where this document was silent, every dependency you added, and anything in this specification you could not meet and why.

## Done

Stop when all of these are true. Do not polish beyond them.

- [ ] The commands in `BUILD.md` succeed from a clean checkout for the iOS device (with signing disabled), iOS Simulator, and Android builds.
- [ ] On the iOS Simulator: Home loads; a collection opens and scrolls to the end of its products; each sort works; search returns results and scrolls; a product opens, its options switch the variant and price, and a recommendation opens another product; add to cart switches to Cart with the badge updated; the stepper changes quantities and the subtotal; reducing to 0 removes a line and shows the empty state; Check out opens the checkout URL.
- [ ] The app launches on an Android emulator and Home loads.
- [ ] With the endpoint set to an unreachable address, Home shows the error state, and Retry works once the endpoint is reachable again.
- [ ] `SHOPBENCH home_ready` appears in the simulator log once per launch.
- [ ] All accessibility identifiers above are present.

#import "SBNative.h"
#import <os/log.h>
#import <UIKit/UIKit.h>
#import <SafariServices/SafariServices.h>

@implementation SBNative

+ (void)logHomeReady {
    os_log(OS_LOG_DEFAULT, "SHOPBENCH home_ready");
}

+ (UIViewController *)topViewController {
    UIWindow *keyWindow = nil;
    for (UIScene *scene in UIApplication.sharedApplication.connectedScenes) {
        if (![scene isKindOfClass:[UIWindowScene class]]) continue;
        for (UIWindow *w in ((UIWindowScene *)scene).windows) {
            if (w.isKeyWindow) { keyWindow = w; break; }
        }
        if (keyWindow) break;
    }
    UIViewController *vc = keyWindow.rootViewController;
    while (vc.presentedViewController) vc = vc.presentedViewController;
    return vc;
}

+ (void)openInAppBrowser:(NSString *)url {
    NSURL *u = [NSURL URLWithString:url];
    if (!u) return;
    SFSafariViewController *safari = [[SFSafariViewController alloc] initWithURL:u];
    [[self topViewController] presentViewController:safari animated:YES completion:nil];
}

@end
EOF
cat > App_Resources/iOS/src/module.modulemap <<'EOF'
module SBNative {
    header "SBNative.h"
    export *
}
EOF

import XCTest

final class Flows: Base {
    func testHome() {
        wait("collection-chip-0"); wait("best-seller-0")
        for id in ["home-scroll", "featured-collection", "collection-card-0", "tab-home", "tab-search", "tab-cart"] { wait(id, 2) }
        shot("home"); dump("home")
        el("home-scroll").swipeUp(); el("home-scroll").swipeUp()
        shot("home-scrolled")
    }

    func testCollection() {
        wait("collection-chip-0").tap()
        wait("product-card-0")
        for id in ["product-grid", "sort-featured", "sort-best-selling", "sort-price-asc", "sort-price-desc", "back"] { wait(id, 2) }
        shot("collection"); dump("collection")
        var maxIdx = 0
        var stable = 0
        while stable < 4 {
            el("product-grid").swipeUp(velocity: .fast)
            var found = maxIdx
            for i in (maxIdx)...(maxIdx + 40) where el("product-card-\(i)").exists { found = i }
            if found == maxIdx { stable += 1 } else { stable = 0; maxIdx = found }
        }
        print("COLLECTION max card index: \(maxIdx)")
        shot("collection-end")
        for s in ["sort-best-selling", "sort-price-asc", "sort-price-desc", "sort-featured"] {
            el(s).tap()
            sleep(1)
            wait("product-card-0")
            shot("collection-\(s)"); dump("collection-\(s)")
        }
        el("back").tap()
        wait("home-scroll")
    }

    func testProduct() {
        wait("best-seller-0").tap()
        let add = wait("add-to-cart")
        wait("product-carousel", 2); wait("back", 2)
        shot("product"); dump("product")
        print("ADD LABEL before: \(add.label)")
        let pills = app.descendants(matching: .any).matching(NSPredicate(format: "identifier BEGINSWITH 'option-'"))
        print("PILLS: \(pills.allElementsBoundByIndex.map { $0.identifier })")
        if pills.count > 1 { pills.element(boundBy: pills.count - 1).tap() }
        sleep(1)
        print("ADD LABEL after: \(el("add-to-cart").label)")
        el("product-carousel").swipeLeft()
        sleep(1)
        shot("product-swiped")
        app.swipeUp(); app.swipeUp()
        shot("product-bottom")
        wait("recommendation-0").tap()
        sleep(3)
        shot("product-rec"); dump("product-rec")
        el("back").tap(); sleep(1)
        el("back").tap()
        wait("home-scroll")
        shot("product-back-home")
    }

    func testCart() {
        wait("tab-cart").tap()
        sleep(1)
        shot("cart-empty")
        wait("tab-home").tap()
        wait("best-seller-1").tap()
        wait("add-to-cart").tap()
        wait("cart-line-0")
        print("BADGE: \(label("cart-badge")) SUBTOTAL: \(label("cart-subtotal"))")
        shot("cart-1"); dump("cart-1")
        el("qty-inc-0").tap()
        sleep(3)
        print("BADGE: \(label("cart-badge")) SUBTOTAL: \(label("cart-subtotal"))")
        shot("cart-2")
        el("checkout").tap()
        sleep(4)
        shot("checkout"); dump("checkout")
        let done = app.buttons["Done"]
        if done.exists { done.tap() } else { app.swipeDown() }
        sleep(2)
        el("qty-dec-0").tap(); sleep(3)
        print("BADGE: \(label("cart-badge")) SUBTOTAL: \(label("cart-subtotal"))")
        el("qty-dec-0").tap(); sleep(3)
        shot("cart-emptied"); dump("cart-emptied")
        print("BADGE exists after empty: \(el("cart-badge").exists)")
    }

    func testSearch() {
        wait("tab-search").tap()
        sleep(1)
        shot("search-empty")
        let f = wait("search-input")
        f.tap()
        f.typeText("shirt")
        wait("search-result-0")

        for _ in 0..<6 { el("search-results").swipeUp(velocity: .fast) }
        var maxIdx = 0
        for i in 0...200 where el("search-result-\(i)").exists { maxIdx = i }
        print("SEARCH max visible index: \(maxIdx)")
        shot("search-scrolled")
        el("search-result-\(maxIdx)").tap()
        wait("add-to-cart")
        shot("search-product")
        el("back").tap()
        wait("search-results")
    }

    func testError() {
        wait("error-retry", 40)
        shot("error"); dump("error")
    }
}

# Building Everbloom (NativeScript)

All commands run from the project root of a clean checkout. The scripts in
`scripts/` are thin wrappers around the NativeScript CLI (`ns`, installed
locally from `package.json`) and `xcodebuild`.

## Prerequisites

- macOS with Xcode 26 (command line tools selected), an iOS Simulator runtime.
- Node.js and npm.
- `/usr/bin/gem` (the system Ruby). The NativeScript CLI merges xcconfig files
  with the Ruby `xcodeproj` gem; `scripts/setup.sh` installs it into the local
  `.gems/` directory, and the build scripts point `GEM_PATH` at it. No system
  gem install is needed. CocoaPods is not used.
- Android: Android SDK (`ANDROID_HOME`) with platform 36 / build-tools 36,
  a JDK 17+ (`JAVA_HOME`), and an emulator or device for running.

## 1. Install dependencies

```sh
./scripts/setup.sh
```

(This runs `npm ci` and `gem install --install-dir .gems xcodeproj -v 1.28.1`.)

## 2. iOS device release build (benchmarked)

Signed build with automatic signing:

```sh
DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=XXXXXXXXXX ./scripts/build-ios-device.sh
```

Without `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` the same command builds with code signing disabled
(`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`):

```sh
./scripts/build-ios-device.sh
```

Result: `build/ios-device/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/nativescript.app`

What the script runs:

```sh
GEM_PATH=$PWD/.gems npx ns prepare ios --release
xcodebuild -project platforms/ios/nativescript.xcodeproj -scheme nativescript \
  -configuration Release -sdk iphoneos -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' \
  -derivedDataPath build/ios-device \
  -allowProvisioningUpdates CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=$DEVELOPMENT_TEAM build
```

## 3. Install and launch on a connected iPhone

```sh
xcrun devicectl list devices                      # find the device identifier
DEVICE=<device identifier>
xcrun devicectl device install app --device "$DEVICE" \
  build/ios-device/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/nativescript.app
xcrun devicectl device process launch --device "$DEVICE" \
  --environment-variables '{"SHOP_API_URL":"http://192.168.1.20:8787/api"}' \
  dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.nativescript
```

Omit `--environment-variables` to use the default endpoint
(`https://apparel-large-catalog.mock.shop/api`). The app writes
`SHOPBENCH home_ready` to the unified log once Home shows loaded content.

## 4. iOS Simulator build

```sh
./scripts/build-ios-sim.sh
```

Result: `build/ios-sim/Build/Products/Release-iphonesimulator/nativescript.app`

Install and launch on the booted simulator:

```sh
xcrun simctl install booted build/ios-sim/Build/Products/Release-iphonesimulator/nativescript.app
SIMCTL_CHILD_SHOP_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/api \
  xcrun simctl launch booted dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.nativescript
```

Watch for the marker:

```sh
xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream --predicate 'eventMessage CONTAINS "SHOPBENCH"'
```

## 5. Android release APK

```sh
./scripts/build-android.sh
```

Result: `build/android/everbloom-release.apk` (release build signed with the
Android debug keystore `~/.android/debug.keystore`; the script creates that
keystore with the standard debug credentials if it does not exist).

The endpoint on Android is a build-time setting. Set `SHOP_API_URL` in the
environment of the build command (it is injected into the bundle by webpack's
DefinePlugin, see `webpack.config.js`):

```sh
SHOP_API_URL=http://192.168.1.20:8787/api ./scripts/build-android.sh
```

(From the Android emulator, the host Mac is `http://10.0.2.2:<port>/api`.)
Without it the default endpoint is used. Install and launch:

```sh
adb install -r build/android/everbloom-release.apk
adb shell am start -n dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.nativescript/com.tns.NativeScriptActivity
```

## 6. Build modes and toolchain

| Target | Mode |
|---|---|
| iOS device | `ns prepare ios --release` (webpack production mode: minified bundle, no dev server/HMR/inspector) + Xcode `Release` configuration, arm64, optimizations on |
| iOS Simulator | Same as device: `ns prepare ios --release` + Xcode `Release` configuration for the simulator SDK. This is the most production-like mode NativeScript supports on the simulator. |
| Android | `ns build android --release` (webpack production mode, Gradle release build), signed with the debug keystore |

The iOS `SHOP_API_URL` launch environment variable is read at startup and takes
priority over any build-time `SHOP_API_URL`.

Toolchain used:

| Tool | Version |
|---|---|
| macOS | 26.5.1 |
| Xcode | 26.6 (17F113), iOS SDK 26.5, Simulator iOS 26.5 (iPhone 17 Pro) |
| Node.js / npm | 26.13.0 / 11.20.0 |
| NativeScript CLI (`nativescript`) | 9.1.2 |
| `@nativescript/core` | 9.1.3 |
| `@nativescript/ios` runtime | 9.1.0 |
| `@nativescript/android` runtime | 9.1.1 |
| `@nativescript/webpack` | 5.0.39 |
| TypeScript | 5.9.3 |
| Ruby (system) / xcodeproj gem | 2.6.10 / 1.28.1 |
| JDK | OpenJDK 21.0.6 (Android Studio JBR) |
| Android | compileSdk/targetSdk 36, build-tools 36, Gradle 8.14.3 (wrapper), emulator image android-36 arm64 |

# Notes

## Project layout

- `app/app.ts`, `app/app-root.xml|ts`: root layout = one `Frame` per tab plus a custom tab bar.
- `app/pages/*`: Home, Collection, Product, Search, Cart (XML + TypeScript code-behind, core `Observable` view models).
- `app/lib/api.ts`: endpoint resolution and the GraphQL documents (copied verbatim from `spec/storefront.graphql`), sent with core `Http.request`.
- `app/lib/cart.ts`: in-memory cart store; `app/lib/paged-list.ts`: infinite scroll for `ListView`; `app/lib/grid.ts`: 2-column grid rows.
- `app/components/icon.ts`: the design's stroke icons drawn natively (CAShapeLayer / Android ShapeDrawable).
- `App_Resources/iOS/src/SBNative.{h,m}`: small Objective-C helper for `os_log` (benchmark marker) and `SFSafariViewController`.

## Dependencies added

None beyond the NativeScript project itself. `package.json` contains only
`@nativescript/core` (runtime) and the NativeScript toolchain packages
(`nativescript` CLI, `@nativescript/ios`, `@nativescript/android`,
`@nativescript/webpack`, `@nativescript/types`, `typescript`). The template's
`@nativescript/theme` was removed.

Build-time only: the Ruby `xcodeproj` gem, which the NativeScript CLI itself
requires to merge xcconfig files; it is installed into `./.gems` by
`scripts/setup.sh`.

The in-app browser uses the system `SFSafariViewController` (SafariServices,
linked via `App_Resources/iOS/build.xcconfig`) instead of a plugin.

## Decisions where the spec is silent

- **Tab bar**: a custom bar (NativeScript `GridLayout`) over three `Frame`s instead of the core `TabView`, because it needs a badge, the design's vector icons, accessibility identifiers per tab, and must hide on the Product screen. The Search and Cart frames are created on first use so that launch only builds Home. Tab switching keeps each frame's stack.
- **Navigation bars**: native action bars are hidden; each screen draws the design's header (44pt). The back button calls `Frame.goBack()`. No transitions beyond NativeScript's default push animation.
- **"See all"** link next to "Collections" in the design is not described in the spec, so it is omitted.
- **Collection header**: nav bar, description and sort chips stay fixed above the scrolling grid (the grid `ListView` is the `product-grid` container).
- **Grid rows**: the grid is a `ListView` whose rows hold two cards, with a fixed row height (image 3:4 + two title lines + price + 20pt gap). Titles are clamped to 2 lines, so all rows are the same height. The loading row at the end has the same height with the spinner at its top.
- **Infinite scroll trigger**: on iOS the table's `contentOffset` is observed (KVO) and the next page is requested when less than one viewport height of content remains below the visible area. On Android it is triggered when a row within one screen of the end is built.
- **Sort change**: clears the grid and shows a spinner until the first page of the new order arrives.
- **Search**: the debounce timer is 300 ms after the last keystroke; the query is trimmed; responses for stale queries (and stale pages) are dropped. While the first page loads a spinner is shown. Result rows are fixed at 101pt (64×85 thumbnail + 8pt padding), titles up to 3 lines.
- **Product carousel**: horizontal `ScrollView` with native paging (`pagingEnabled`) on iOS; on Android it snaps to the nearest page after scrolling stops. Page dots are hidden when there is only one image. The round back button stays fixed over the top-left corner while the page scrolls.
- **Option pills** wrap onto multiple lines when they do not fit. Selecting a value picks the variant matching all currently selected options with that one changed; if no variant matches exactly, the first variant having that value is selected.
- **Prices**: the product price uses the `sale` color when the selected variant's compare-at price is higher, with the compare-at price struck through next to it. Recommendation cards follow the same rule as product cards. (No product in the catalog has variants with different prices, so switching variants changes the selection and labels but the price stays the same in practice.)
- **Add to cart**: the button is disabled while the request is in flight; on success the app switches to the Cart tab. On a network failure an alert ("Couldn't update cart" / "Check your connection and try again.") is shown and the tab is not switched.
- **Cart mutations** are serialized. Stepper taps are applied as +1/−1 against the latest cart returned by the server, so rapid taps are not lost. Network failures show the same alert as above.
- **Empty cart**: the "Start shopping" button switches to the Home tab.
- **Error state**: shown on Home, Collection, Search and Product when the request fails (HTTP error, GraphQL response without `data`, or a 30 s timeout). Retry repeats the request. The cart has no load request, so it has no error state.
- **Loading states**: Home shows the design's skeleton on the first frame; Collection, Search and Product show a centered spinner.
- **Status bar / safe areas**: scrolling content stays below the status bar; only the product image carousel extends under it.
- **Images**: core `Image` with `loadMode="async"` and `stretch="aspectFill"`; the placeholder is the `surface` color behind the image.
- **App name / IDs**: the Xcode project and `.app` are named `nativescript` (NativeScript derives this from the project directory name); the display name is `Everbloom` and the bundle/application ID is `dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.nativescript`.
- **App icon**: the NativeScript template's default icon is left as is (no custom icon). The launch screen is plain white (template images removed) on both platforms.
- **Endpoint override**: iOS reads `SHOP_API_URL` from the process environment at launch. A build-time `SHOP_API_URL` (webpack `DefinePlugin`) is supported on both platforms and is what Android uses; the iOS launch variable wins if both are set.
- **Plain HTTP**: iOS `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads` + `NSAllowsLocalNetworking`; Android `usesCleartextTraffic` and a network security config permitting cleartext.
- **Portrait only, iPhone only** (`UIDeviceFamily` 1); light appearance forced (`UIUserInterfaceStyle` Light) since dark mode is out of scope.
- **Logging**: the only log written by app code is `SHOPBENCH home_ready` via `os_log` (default level), once per process, scheduled right after the loaded Home content is bound. Release webpack builds also strip any `console.*` calls. The NativeScript iOS runtime prints one "Runtime initialization took …" line to stdout at startup; that is NativeScript's own output and does not go to the unified log.

## NativeScript ListView workarounds (iOS)

Getting the lazily rendered lists to behave under scrolling and XCUITest needed some care; these are worth knowing when reading `app/lib/paged-list.ts` and `app/lib/grid.ts`:

1. **Fixed `rowHeight`.** Without it, NativeScript measures rows with a separate measurement pass that re-binds views and left cells with stale data/identifiers.
2. **Rows are filled imperatively in `itemLoading`** (no `{{ }}` bindings inside the row templates). Bindings inside recycled cells were unreliable for some properties (image `src`, `testID`).
3. **Cell views are kept attached to their cells.** When a `UITableViewCell` leaves the window NativeScript tears down its item view and rebuilds it when the cell is reused; that rebuild threw inside `cellForRowAtIndexPath` and UIKit aborted the app. The app overrides `_removeContainer` on its own `ListView` instances (no change to NativeScript itself) so each item view simply stays with its reusable cell.

`scripts/setup.sh`.

linked via `App_Resources/iOS/build.xcconfig`) instead of a plugin.

- **Navigation bars**: native action bars are hidden; each screen draws the design's header (44pt). The back button calls `Frame.goBack()`. No transitions beyond NativeScript's default push animation.
- **"See all"** link next to "Collections" in the design is not described in the spec, so it is omitted.
- **Collection header**: nav bar, description and sort chips stay fixed above the scrolling grid (the grid `ListView` is the `product-grid` container).
- **Grid rows**: the grid is a `ListView` whose rows hold two cards, with a fixed row height (image 3:4 + two title lines + price + 20pt gap). Titles are clamped to 2 lines, so all rows are the same height. The loading row at the end has the same height with the spinner at its top.
- **Infinite scroll trigger**: on iOS the table's `contentOffset` is observed (KVO) and the next page is requested when less than one viewport height of content remains below the visible area. On Android it is triggered when a row within one screen of the end is built.
- **Sort change**: clears the grid and shows a spinner until the first page of the new order arrives.
- **Search**: the debounce timer is 300 ms after the last keystroke; the query is trimmed; responses for stale queries (and stale pages) are dropped. While the first page loads a spinner is shown. Result rows are fixed at 101pt (64×85 thumbnail + 8pt padding), titles up to 3 lines.
- **Product carousel**: horizontal `ScrollView` with native paging (`pagingEnabled`) on iOS; on Android it snaps to the nearest page after scrolling stops. Page dots are hidden when there is only one image. The round back button stays fixed over the top-left corner while the page scrolls.
- **Option pills** wrap onto multiple lines when they do not fit. Selecting a value picks the variant matching all currently selected options with that one changed; if no variant matches exactly, the first variant having that value is selected.
- **Prices**: the product price uses the `sale` color when the selected variant's compare-at price is higher, with the compare-at price struck through next to it. Recommendation cards follow the same rule as product cards. (No product in the catalog has variants with different prices, so switching variants changes the selection and labels but the price stays the same in practice.)
- **Add to cart**: the button is disabled while the request is in flight; on success the app switches to the Cart tab. On a network failure an alert ("Couldn't update cart" / "Check your connection and try again.") is shown and the tab is not switched.
- **Cart mutations** are serialized. Stepper taps are applied as +1/−1 against the latest cart returned by the server, so rapid taps are not lost. Network failures show the same alert as above.
- **Empty cart**: the "Start shopping" button switches to the Home tab.
- **Error state**: shown on Home, Collection, Search and Product when the request fails (HTTP error, GraphQL response without `data`, or a 30 s timeout). Retry repeats the request. The cart has no load request, so it has no error state.
- **Loading states**: Home shows the design's skeleton on the first frame; Collection, Search and Product show a centered spinner.
- **Status bar / safe areas**: scrolling content stays below the status bar; only the product image carousel extends under it.
- **Images**: core `Image` with `loadMode="async"` and `stretch="aspectFill"`; the placeholder is the `surface` color behind the image.
- **App name / IDs**: the Xcode project and `.app` are named `nativescript` (NativeScript derives this from the project directory name); the display name is `Everbloom` and the bundle/application ID is `dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.nativescript`.
- **App icon**: the NativeScript template's default icon is left as is (no custom icon). The launch screen is plain white (template images removed) on both platforms.

- **Portrait only, iPhone only** (`UIDeviceFamily` 1); light appearance forced (`UIUserInterfaceStyle` Light) since dark mode is out of scope.
- **Logging**: the only log written by app code is `SHOPBENCH home_ready` via `os_log` (default level), once per process, scheduled right after the loaded Home content is bound. #!/bin/bash
# iOS device (arm64) Release build. Signs automatically with $DEVELOPMENT_TEAM;
# without it, builds with code signing disabled.
set -euo pipefail
source "$(dirname "$0")/env.sh"
npx ns prepare ios --release
SIGNING=(CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO)
if [ -n "${DEVELOPMENT_TEAM:-}" ]; then
  SIGNING=(-allowProvisioningUpdates CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic "DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=$DEVELOPMENT_TEAM")
fi
# NativeScript names the Xcode project after the project directory.
PROJ="$(basename platforms/ios/*.xcodeproj .xcodeproj)"
xcodebuild -project "platforms/ios/$PROJ.xcodeproj" -scheme "$PROJ" \
  -configuration Release -sdk iphoneos -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' \
  -derivedDataPath build/ios-device "${SIGNING[@]}" build
rm -rf "build/ios-device/Everbloom.app"
ditto "build/ios-device/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/$PROJ.app" "build/ios-device/Everbloom.app"
echo "Built: $ROOT/build/ios-device/Everbloom.app"

content.text:
The clean-built simulator app loads Home and logs `SHOPBENCH home_ready` once. (Something else on this machine reinstalled the older build in between, which is why my previous check found the wrong binary. The simulator and Android emulator seem to be shared with another session.)

The Everbloom app is built with NativeScript 9.1 (plain TypeScript and XML on `@nativescript/core`), and every item on the spec's Done list checks out on the iOS Simulator and Android emulator. The device build compiles but hasn't run on a real iPhone.

**What was verified:**
- **Clean checkout:** the BUILD.md commands succeed from a fresh copy for the iOS device build (with signing disabled), the iOS Simulator build and the Android release APK.
- **iOS Simulator (release build):** I drove each flow with an XCUITest harness (kept in my scratchpad, not shipped), which also confirms the accessibility identifiers are visible to XCUITest:
  - Home loads.
  - A collection scrolls to the end: all 84 products, matching the API count.
  - All four sorts reorder the list.
  - Search pages through all 67 results for "shirt".
  - Options change the selected variant, and a recommendation opens another product.
  - The tab bar hides on Product and comes back afterwards.
  - Add to cart switches to Cart with the badge set to 1. The stepper changes the subtotal ($120 → $240 → $120), going to 0 shows the empty state, and Check out opens the checkout page in an in-app Safari view.
- **Error state:** with `SHOP_API_URL` pointing at an endpoint that was down, Home shows the error screen, and Retry loads it once the endpoint comes up.
- **Log marker:** `SHOPBENCH home_ready` appears exactly once per launch. App code writes nothing else to the system log.
- **Android:** the release APK launches and Home loads. Retry also worked after the emulator's flaky DNS caused one failed load.

**Things you should know:**
- **Ruby gem:** the NativeScript CLI needs the Ruby `xcodeproj` gem for any iOS build. `scripts/setup.sh` installs it into a local `.gems/` folder, and the scripts reach it through a small `scripts/bin/ruby` wrapper. Setting `GEM_PATH` globally broke CocoaPods, which the CLI also checks for.
- **App path:** NativeScript names the Xcode project after the folder, so the scripts copy the built app to a fixed `build/ios-device/Everbloom.app` (and `build/ios-sim/Everbloom.app`).
- **ListView workarounds:** NativeScript's iOS ListView crashed the app during scrolling. When a recycled cell was brought back, rebuilding its content threw inside UIKit's cell-preparation call and UIKit aborted. I worked around it from app code without modifying NativeScript:
  - fixed row heights
  - filling rows in code instead of data bindings
  - keeping each row's view attached to its cell
  - loading the next page based on scroll position

  Details are in NOTES.md.
- **Variant prices:** no product in the catalog has variants with different prices, so switching options updates the selection and labels but the price never actually changes.
- **Android gaps:** Check out opens the system browser instead of an in-app one, and the system gesture bar overlaps the bottom of the tab bar on the API 36 emulator.
- **Dependencies:** none added beyond NativeScript itself. The in-app browser uses Apple's built-in Safari view through a small Objective-C helper.

Everything is in `/Users/itome/shopbench-runs/nativescript`. BUILD.md has the commands and toolchain versions; NOTES.md has the decisions and caveats.
